steps.explain: \(Q\) is on line \(ON\): \(\overrightarrow{OQ}=\overrightarrow{ON}+\overrightarrow{NQ}=\underset{\sim}{n}+\lambda\underset{\sim}{n}\).

\(\overrightarrow{PQ}=\overrightarrow{OQ}-\overrightarrow{OP}=(1+\lambda)\underset{\sim}{n}-(2\underset{\sim}{n}-\underset{\sim}{m})\). And \(\overrightarrow{MN}=\underset{\sim}{n}-\underset{\sim}{m}\) (end minus start).

Perpendicular: \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{MN}=0\). Expand, using \(\underset{\sim}{n}\cdot\underset{\sim}{n}=|\underset{\sim}{n}|^{2}\), \(\underset{\sim}{m}\cdot\underset{\sim}{m}=|\underset{\sim}{m}|^{2}\), \(\underset{\sim}{m}\cdot\underset{\sim}{n}=\underset{\sim}{n}\cdot\underset{\sim}{m}\).
Collect the \(\lambda\) terms on one side.
Divide by \(|\underset{\sim}{n}|^{2}-\underset{\sim}{m}\cdot\underset{\sim}{n}\) (not zero, or \(N\) would coincide with the foot of the perpendicular).

Why not the others: B takes \(\overrightarrow{OQ}=\lambda\underset{\sim}{n}\) (but \(\overrightarrow{NQ}=\lambda\underset{\sim}{n}\), so \(\overrightarrow{OQ}=(1+\lambda)\underset{\sim}{n}\)); C uses \(\underset{\sim}{p}=\underset{\sim}{n}+\underset{\sim}{m}\) (wrong midpoint relation); D uses parallel instead of perpendicular.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: \(\underset{\sim}{p}=2\underset{\sim}{n}-\underset{\sim}{m}\); \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{MN}=0\).

questions.stem: \(OABC\) is a parallelogram. \(\overrightarrow{OA}\) is represented by the vector \(\underset{\sim}{a}\) and \(\overrightarrow{OC}\) is represented by the vector \(\underset{\sim}{c}\). \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\) and \(N\) is the point on \(OB\) such that \(ON:NB=2:1\). Find expressions for \(\overrightarrow{ON}\), \(\overrightarrow{OM}\), \(\overrightarrow{AN}\) and \(\overrightarrow{AM}\), given your answers in simplest form. Which set is correct?

questions.hint: Write every vector by travelling along known vectors from \(O\). In a PARALLELOGRAM \(\overrightarrow{OB}=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{c}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CB}=\underset{\sim}{a}\). Then \(\overrightarrow{AN}=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OA}\) (END minus START).

steps.explain: \(OB\) is the diagonal: \(\overrightarrow{OB}=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{c}\). \(ON:NB=2:1\) means \(N\) is \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of the way from \(O\) to \(B\).

steps.explain: \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\): go to \(C\) then half of \(\overrightarrow{CB}=\underset{\sim}{a}\).
\(\overrightarrow{AN}=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OA}=\dfrac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{a}+\dfrac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{a}\).
\(\overrightarrow{AM}=\overrightarrow{OM}-\overrightarrow{OA}=\dfrac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{a}\).

questions.hint: Three points \(A,N,M\) are COLLINEAR if \(\overrightarrow{AM}\) is a scalar MULTIPLE of \(\overrightarrow{AN}\) (parallel vectors) AND they share the common point \(A\).

steps.explain: Both vectors contain the same vector \((2\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{a})\).
Express \(\overrightarrow{AM}\) as a multiple of \(\overrightarrow{AN}\): \(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{3}}=\dfrac{3}{2}\).

In parallelogram \(OMPN\): \(\overrightarrow{MP}=\overrightarrow{ON}\) (opposite sides equal and parallel), so \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\overrightarrow{OM}+\overrightarrow{MP}=\overrightarrow{OM}+\overrightarrow{ON}\).
Add the components.

questions.stem: Show that the area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides \(\underset{\sim}{u}\) and \(\underset{\sim}{v}\) is \(\dfrac{\left|\,|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\underset{\sim}{v}-(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u})\underset{\sim}{u}\,\right|}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|}\). Which argument is correct?
options: Area \(=\) base \(\times\) perpendicular height \(=|\underset{\sim}{u}|\times\left|\underset{\sim}{v}-\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}\right|\), where \(\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}=\dfrac{\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u}}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}}\underset{\sim}{u}\). So area \(=|\underset{\sim}{u}|\left|\underset{\sim}{v}-\dfrac{(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u})\underset{\sim}{u}}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}}\right|=\dfrac{\left||\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\underset{\sim}{v}-(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u})\underset{\sim}{u}\right|}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|}\).

Area \(=\) base \(\times\) height, with height \(=\left|\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}\right|\) (the component of \(\underset{\sim}{v}\) ALONG \(\underset{\sim}{u}\)). Substituting \(\text{proj}=\dfrac{\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u}}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}}\underset{\sim}{u}\) gives the formula.

Area \(=|\underset{\sim}{u}||\underset{\sim}{v}|\cos\theta\) where \(\theta\) is the angle between the sides, and \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}}{|\underset{\sim}{u}||\underset{\sim}{v}|}\), so area \(=\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}\); this equals the formula.

Area \(=\dfrac{1}{2}\) base \(\times\) height (the area of a triangle), with height \(=\left|\underset{\sim}{v}-\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}\right|\); doubling gives the formula.
questions.hint: Area of a parallelogram \(=\) base \(\times\) PERPENDICULAR height. Take the base \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|\). The perpendicular height is the length of \(\underset{\sim}{v}\) minus its projection onto \(\underset{\sim}{u}\).

steps.explain: Base \(=|\underset{\sim}{u}|\). The vector \(\underset{\sim}{v}\) splits into a part ALONG \(\underset{\sim}{u}\) (its projection) and a part PERPENDICULAR to \(\underset{\sim}{u}\).
The perpendicular part is \(\underset{\sim}{v}\) minus the projection, and its LENGTH is the height of the parallelogram.
Area \(=\) base \(\times\) height.

Bring the factor \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|\) inside the modulus: put everything over the common denominator \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\), so that \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|\cdot\dfrac{1}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|}\).

Why not the others: B uses the PROJECTION as the height (that is the length ALONG the base, not perpendicular to it); C uses \(\cos\theta\) (the dot product), which does not give an area (the area uses \(\sin\theta\)); D is the area of a TRIANGLE (half).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: Show that the area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides
keyPoints.note: Area \(=|u|\times\) perpendicular height; \(h=|v-\text{proj}_u v|\).

questions.hint: Use the formula \(A=\dfrac{\left||\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\underset{\sim}{v}-(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u})\underset{\sim}{u}\right|}{|\underset{\sim}{u}|}\) with \(\underset{\sim}{u}=(1,\tan\beta)\), \(\underset{\sim}{v}=(1,\tan\alpha)\). Let \(a=\tan\alpha\) and \(b=\tan\beta\) to keep the algebra short.

steps.explain: Compute \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\) and \(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u}\) with \(a=\tan\alpha\), \(b=\tan\beta\).
Compute \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|^{2}\underset{\sim}{v}-(\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u})\underset{\sim}{u}\) component by component.
Simplify: \(x\)-component \(=b(b-a)\); \(y\)-component \(=a-b\).
Its length: \(|a-b|\sqrt{b^{2}+1}\). Divide by \(|\underset{\sim}{u}|=\sqrt{1+b^{2}}\): the square roots cancel.
From the diagram \(\alpha>\beta\) so \(\tan\alpha>\tan\beta\) (tangent is increasing on \(0<\theta<\dfrac\pi2\)), and the absolute value can be dropped.

parts.stem: Find the coordinates of \(F\).
parts.hint: Write |OF| = |DF| = |EF| = 1 as equations in x, y, z and subtract pairs.

steps.explain: Let \(F=(x,y,z)\). All edges have length 1: \(|OF|=|DF|=|EF|=1\).
Subtract the two equations.
Use \(|EF|=1\) with \(E\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2},0\right)\) and compare with \(|OF|=1\).
Subtract: \(-\sqrt3y+\frac34=\frac14\).
Find \(z\) (positive, since \(F\) is above the plane). \(F\) is directly above the centroid \(G\) of the base.

parts.stem:
The vectors \(\overrightarrow{AE}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BG}\) intersect at \(V\). \(V\) is joined to \(O\), \(A\), \(D\) and \(B\) to create a square pyramid.
Using vectors, calculate the angle that one of the triangular faces of the pyramid makes with the base, to the nearest degree.
parts.hint: Use vectors from the midpoint of a base edge: one up the face to V, one across the base to the centre.

steps.explain: The diagonals of the box meet at its centre.

Take face \(VBD\). Its base edge \(BD\) has midpoint \(M=(2,4,0)\). \(VM\) (in the face) and \(NM\) (in the base, from the base centre \(N=(2,2,0)\)) are both perpendicular to \(BD\), so the angle between them is the angle between the face and the base.

parts.stem: Show that the longest diagonal in a cube with side length \(a\) units is \(\sqrt{3}\,a\) units.
parts.answer: Take opposite corners \((0,0,0)\) and \((a,a,a)\). The distance between them is \(\sqrt{a^2+a^2+a^2}=\sqrt{3a^2}=\sqrt{3}\,a\).
parts.hint: Take two opposite corners of the cube and find the distance between them.

steps.explain: Place the cube with one corner at the origin. The opposite corner is then \((a,a,a)\), and the segment joining them is the longest diagonal.
Use the distance formula in three dimensions.
Simplify, using \(a>0\).

questions.stem: What is the distance of the point \((2,3,7)\) from the \(x\)-\(z\) plane?
questions.hint: The \(x\)-\(z\) plane is the plane \(y=0\). The distance of a point from it is the absolute value of its \(y\)-coordinate.

steps.explain: The \(xz\)-plane contains every point whose \(y\)-coordinate is 0.
Moving straight from \((2,3,7)\) to the plane means changing only \(y\) from 3 to 0: the point becomes \((2,0,7)\).
Distance.
Why not 2 or 7? Those are the distances from the \(yz\)-plane and the \(xy\)-plane.

questions.stem: Let the line \(l\) have parametric equations \(x=3-\lambda\), \(y=2+2\lambda\) and \(z=5-2\lambda\). Find the distance from the line to the point \(R=3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}\).
questions.hint: Pick a point \(P\) on the line (try \(\lambda=0\)), form \(\overrightarrow{PR}\), and remove its component ALONG the line: the leftover (perpendicular) part is the distance. Use \(d^2=|\overrightarrow{PR}|^2-(\text{projection})^2\).

steps.explain: Point on the line (\(\lambda=0\)) and direction.
Vector from \(P\) to \(R\).
Component of \(\overrightarrow{PR}\) ALONG the line: \(\dfrac{\overrightarrow{PR}\cdot\mathbf{d}}{|\mathbf{d}|}\).
Pythagoras: distance² = length² − projection².
Take the square root.
Check with the cross product: \(\dfrac{|\overrightarrow{PR}\times\mathbf{d}|}{|\mathbf{d}|}=\dfrac{|(12,6,0)|}{3}=\dfrac{6\sqrt{5}}{3}=2\sqrt{5}\) ✓.

keyPoints.note: Remove the component of PR along the line direction.

steps.explain: \(\overrightarrow{AB}=B-A=(-1,2,1)\), so \(|AB|=\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+2^{2}+1^{2}}=\sqrt6\). The three sides are \(\sqrt2,\ \sqrt6,\ 2\sqrt2\): all different, so the triangle is SCALENE.
Pythagoras check: \(|OA|^{2}+|AB|^{2}=2+6=8=|OB|^{2}\), so the RIGHT angle is at \(A\) (opposite the longest side \(OB\)), not at \(O\).

A \(1:\sqrt3:2\) right triangle is the \(30^{\circ}\)-\(60^{\circ}\)-\(90^{\circ}\) triangle. Angle \(AOB\): \(\cos\angle AOB=\dfrac{|OA|}{|OB|}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(\angle AOB=60^{\circ}\). Then \(\angle OBA=30^{\circ}\).

Check each option: A false (\(\angle AOB=60^{\circ}\), the right angle is at \(A\)); B false (scalene); C false (\(\angle OAB=90^{\circ}\) is three times \(\angle OBA=30^{\circ}\), not twice); D true (\(60^{\circ}=2\times30^{\circ}\)).
So the correct choice is option D.

questions.stem: A sphere is defined by \(\left|\underset{\sim}{r}-\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\ 5\end{pmatrix}\right|=4\sqrt3\). Which of the following points lie outside of the sphere?
questions.hint: The sphere has CENTRE \((2,-3,5)\) and radius \(4\sqrt3\), so \(r^{2}=48\). A point is OUTSIDE when its distance from the centre is GREATER than the radius: compare \(d^{2}\) with 48.

steps.explain: Radius squared: \(\left(4\sqrt3\right)^{2}=16\times3=48\). Compute \(d^{2}=(x-2)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+(z-5)^{2}\) for each point.
So only \((1,0,-3)\) lies outside the sphere.
So the correct choice is option D.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of \(P\) that divides the interval \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3\), where \(A=(1,3,4)\) and \(B=(-4,8,2)\).
questions.hint: Dividing \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3\) means \(AP:PB=2:3\), so \(P\) is \(\dfrac{2}{2+3}=\dfrac{2}{5}\) of the way from \(A\) to \(B\): \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\overrightarrow{OA}+\dfrac{2}{5}\overrightarrow{AB}\).

steps.explain: \(\overrightarrow{AB}=B-A=(-4-1,\ 8-3,\ 2-4)\).
\(\dfrac{2}{5}\overrightarrow{AB}=\left(-2,\ 2,\ -\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\).
Add to \(A\).
Why not the others: B is the point \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of the way from \(A\) (\(AP:PB=3:2\)); C and D use wrong fractions (e.g. the midpoint-type \(\dfrac{1}{2}\)).
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: \(P\left(-1,5,\dfrac{16}{5}\right)\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3\), where \(A=(1,3,4)\) and \(B=(-4,8,2)\). Check the result by calculating \(\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\right|\) and \(\left|\overrightarrow{AP}\right|\).
questions.hint: If \(AP:PB=2:3\) then \(AP\) is \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) of \(AB\): check \(|AP|=\dfrac{2}{5}|AB|\). Calculate each length with \(\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}\) (and simplify surds).

steps.explain: \(\overrightarrow{AP}=P-A=\left(-2,2,-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\): \(|AP|=\sqrt{4+4+\dfrac{16}{25}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{216}{25}}=\dfrac{6\sqrt6}{5}\).
Ratio: \(\dfrac{|AP|}{|AB|}=\dfrac{\dfrac{6\sqrt6}{5}}{3\sqrt6}=\dfrac{6}{15}=\dfrac{2}{5}\). So \(AP:PB=2:3\) ✓.
Why not the others: B, D confuse lengths with squared lengths or give the wrong ratio.
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: If \(\underset{\sim}{P}=\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{k}\) and \(\underset{\sim}{R}=9\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}+8\underset{\sim}{k}\), find the point \(Q\) on \(\overrightarrow{PR}\) such that \(PQ:QR=2:3\).
questions.hint: \(PQ:QR=2:3\) means \(Q\) is \(\dfrac{2}{2+3}=\dfrac{2}{5}\) of the way from \(P\) to \(R\): \(\underset{\sim}{Q}=\underset{\sim}{P}+\dfrac{2}{5}\overrightarrow{PR}\).

steps.explain: Find the vector \(\overrightarrow{PR}=\underset{\sim}{R}-\underset{\sim}{P}\).
The whole interval \(PR\) is split into \(2+3=5\) equal parts. \(PQ\) takes 2 of them, so \(\overrightarrow{PQ}=\dfrac{2}{5}\overrightarrow{PR}\).
Position of \(Q\): \(\underset{\sim}{Q}=\underset{\sim}{P}+\overrightarrow{PQ}\). Add \(P=(1,1,1)\) to each component (\(1=\dfrac{5}{5}\)).
Check with the section formula \(Q=\dfrac{3P+2R}{5}=\dfrac{(3+18,\ 3+6,\ 3+16)}{5}=\left(\dfrac{21}5,\dfrac{9}{5},\dfrac{19}5\right)\) ✓.
Why not the others: B uses the ratio \(3:2\) (the wrong way round); C is the midpoint (ratio \(1:1\)); D is only the vector \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\), not the POINT (you must add \(P\)).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: \(Q=P+\dfrac{2}{5}\overrightarrow{PR}\).

options: Let \(N=(p,q,r)\). Each vector is (end) \(-\) (start): \(\overrightarrow{NA}=(1-p,-q,-r)\), \(\overrightarrow{NB}=(-p,1-q,-r)\), \(\overrightarrow{ND}=(-p,-q,1-r)\), \(\overrightarrow{NE}=(1-p,1-q,1-r)\). The sum is \((2-4p,\ 2-4q,\ 2-4r)=\underset{\sim}{0}\), so \(p=q=r=\dfrac{1}{2}\).

Let \(N=(p,q,r)\). \(\overrightarrow{NA}=(1-p,-q,-r)\), \(\overrightarrow{NB}=(-p,1-q,-r)\), \(\overrightarrow{ND}=(-p,-q,1-r)\); leaving out \(\overrightarrow{NE}\), the sum is \((1-3p,1-3q,1-3r)=\underset{\sim}{0}\), so \(p=q=r=\dfrac{1}{3}\).
Let \(N=(p,q,r)\). The sum is \((2-4p,\ 2-4q,\ 2-4r)=\underset{\sim}{0}\), so \(4p=2\Rightarrow p=2\), \(q=2\), \(r=2\).
Let \(N=(p,q,r)\) and use \(\overrightarrow{AN}\) instead: the sum is \((4p-2,4q-2,4r-2)\), so \(N=(1,1,1)\).
questions.hint: Let \(N=(p,q,r)\). Each vector from \(N\) is (end point) \(-\) (\(N\)). Add the four vectors COMPONENT BY COMPONENT and set the \(x\)-, \(y\)- and \(z\)-sums equal to zero.

steps.explain: Write each vector as (end point) \(-\) (start point \(N\)).
Add the four vectors. \(x\)-components: \((1-p)+(-p)+(-p)+(1-p)=2-4p\). Similarly for \(y\) and \(z\).

steps.explain: Solve each equation.
So \(N=\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\), the average of the coordinates of the four vertices. (In the diagram the four vectors from \(N\) to the vertices balance out.)

Why not the others: B leaves out \(\overrightarrow{NE}\) (all four vectors must be included); C solves \(2-4p=0\) incorrectly; D uses \(\overrightarrow{AN}\) (the reverse vectors), which gives the same equation but then \(4p-2=0\) means \(p=\dfrac{1}{2}\), not 1.
So the correct choice is option A.
